t: This is Lombard House, a Grade II listed town mansion filling an entire island block in Mayfair, bounded by Curzon Street, Trebeck Street, Shepherds Market and Hertford Street. It was built between 1901 and 1904 for Charles Spencer-Churchill, the 9th Duke of Marlborough, and his American heiress wife Consuelo Vanderbilt. Her father, William Kissam Vanderbilt, paid for the site and the construction. The Duke, known as Sunny, commissioned it. After the First World War, it served briefly as the temporary London headquarters of the League of Nations.
